mainTopic: How a change to a stolen item affects what a גזלן pays, which kinds of change count, and the view that a change does not alter an item's status (שינוי במקומו עומד).
overview: The משנה teaches that a גזלן always pays what the stolen item was worth at the time of the גזילה. This holds whether he turned wood into vessels or wool into garments, or the animal gave birth or was sheared while he had it. The גמרא infers that only a real change counts, not sanding or washing. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite. אביי answers that the משנה teaches a reversible, rabbinic-level change and the ברייתא a permanent, Torah-level one. רב אשי answers that both speak of permanent changes. The גמרא then asks whether washing wool is a change at all, using the laws of ראשית הגז, and אביי, רבא and רבי חייא בר אבין each answer differently. A further question about dyeing in רבי שמעון's view leads to the distinction between dye that soap removes and indigo, which is permanent. Finally אביי lists five תנאים who hold שינוי במקומו עומד, and the גמרא starts proving each one. The proof for בית שמאי, from a prostitute's payment that she changed, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Stolen wood or wool turned into products
steps.stepSummary: A robber who turns stolen wood into vessels, or stolen wool into garments, pays the value from the time of the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone steals wood and makes vessels from it, or steals wool and makes garments from it, he pays what it was worth when he stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a robber who changed the stolen material into something new. He pays its original value instead of giving back the finished product.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making vessels or garments is a real שינוי (change). Because of that change, the robber now owns the item. He owes the victim money equal to the raw material's value at the moment of the גזילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A change in the item that lets the robber acquire it
According to the value at the time of the robbery

steps.confusionAlert: The robber does not get away free. He still has to pay. The change only means he pays money instead of returning the actual object.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who robs wood
and made it into vessels,
or wool and made it into garments –
pays according to the time of the robbery.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turning stolen raw material into a new product is a שינוי, so the robber keeps the product and pays the value from the time of the גזילה.

steps.title: Stealing an animal that was already pregnant or full of wool
steps.stepSummary: If the cow was already pregnant or the ewe already full of wool when stolen, the robber pays for a cow about to give birth or a ewe ready for shearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone steals a pregnant cow and it gives birth, or a ewe full of wool and he shears it, he pays the price of a cow about to give birth and a ewe ready to be sheared.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to animals that already carried extra value (an unborn calf, a full coat of wool) at the time they were stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unborn calf and the wool were part of the animal's value when it was stolen, so that value is included in the payment. Since the calf was born and the wool was sheared while the animal was with the robber, they stay with him, and he pays for them through this higher price.

phrases.english: If he robbed a pregnant cow – and it gave birth,
or a ewe laden with wool – and he sheared it;
he pays the value of a cow ready to give birth,
and the value of a ewe ready to be sheared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same principle (value at the time of the robbery) to animals that already carried extra value when stolen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The robber pays the higher value the animal had at the time of the גזילה, since the pregnancy and the wool already existed then.

steps.title: Animal that got pregnant or grew wool while with the robber
steps.stepSummary: If the pregnancy or wool developed only while the robber had the animal, he pays only the animal's original value.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone steals a cow and it becomes pregnant with him and gives birth, or a ewe that grows wool with him and he shears it, he pays what it was worth when he stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: the extra value grew only after the robbery. The robber pays just the original value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare this with the previous step. There, the extra value existed at the time of the robbery, so he paid for it. Here, the growth happened while the robber had the animal, so it is not counted in the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: And it became pregnant while with him
And it became laden with wool while with him

phrases.english: If he robbed a cow – and it became pregnant while with him and gave birth,
or a ewe – and it became laden with wool while with him and he sheared it;
he pays according to the time of the robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 2: here the added value appeared only after the robbery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Growth that happens while the animal is with the robber is not included. He pays the value from the time of the גזילה.

steps.title: The general rule: robbers pay the value at the time of the robbery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up all its cases: every robber pays according to the value at the time of the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: all robbers pay according to the value at the time they stole.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up its cases with one general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three cases (changed material, an animal stolen pregnant, an animal that became pregnant later) follow one rule. The moment of the גזילה fixes the amount owed, and later changes in value do not affect it.
steps.whatToRemember: A גזלן always pays what the item was worth when he stole it, no matter what happened to it afterward.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
All robbers pay according to the time of the robbery.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The time of the גזילה sets the payment for every robber.

steps.title: Only a significant change counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that making vessels or garments is a real change, but sanding wood or washing wool is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: wood made into vessels, yes; wood that was only sanded, no. Wool made into garments, yes; wool that was only washed, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing an inference from the משנה's exact cases. They show how big a change must be before the robber acquires the stolen item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה chose full transformations: vessels from wood, garments from wool. That choice implies that a light change, such as sanding the wood or washing the wool, is not enough of a שינוי. In those cases the robber must return the item itself.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean sanding or washing has no legal effect at all. It means these changes are not big enough for the robber to acquire the item. He must give it back.

phrases.english: GEMARA: They say:
wood that he made into vessels – yes,
phrases.notes: "Yes" means this counts as a change, so the robber acquires it.

phrases.english: if he sanded it – no;
wool that he made into garments – yes,
if he washed it – no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first case of the משנה (step 1) and infers how big a change must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a significant change, like making vessels or garments, lets the robber acquire the item. Sanding or washing does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא that treats sanding and washing as a change
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that sanding wood, smoothing stones, washing wool or cleaning flax counts as a change, which contradicts the inference from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: If someone stole wood and sanded it, stones and smoothed them, wool and washed it, or flax and cleaned it, he pays according to the value at the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with what it just inferred from the משנה in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא inferred that sanding wood or washing wool is NOT a real change. This ברייתא says the robber 'pays as at the time of the robbery' after exactly those acts. That means they DO count as a change, so the robber keeps the item and pays only its original value.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they raised a contradiction': a source is brought that clashes with what was just said
He smoothed or chiseled them (the stones)
He whitened it, meaning he washed or bleached the wool

steps.confusionAlert: 'He pays according to the time of the robbery' is the sign that the change counted. The robber keeps the changed item and pays only its original value.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
If he robbed wood and sanded it,
stones and smoothed them,
wool and washed it,
phrases.notes: Literally 'whitened it.' Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: flax and cleaned it –
he pays according to the time of the robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that sanding wood or washing wool is not a real change.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules that after these exact acts the robber pays the value at the time of the robbery. That shows they count as a change.

steps.title: אביי: The משנה teaches a reversible change
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה is teaching a rabbinic-level change, one that can be undone. A Torah-level change is then included all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Our תנא teaches a rabbinic change, one that can be undone, and all the more so a Torah change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins answering the contradiction by saying the משנה is talking about a weaker kind of change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of change. A שינוי דרבנן can be undone, and it works only because the חכמים made it count. A שינוי דאורייתא cannot be undone, and it works by Torah law. אביי says the משנה picked the weaker kind to teach a bigger lesson, so the stronger kind is obviously included.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
A change that counts only by rabbinic law
That goes back, meaning the change can be undone
A change that counts by Torah law, one that cannot be undone

steps.whyThisMatters: This split between a reversible rabbinic change and an irreversible Torah change is the key that solves the whole contradiction.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The tanna of our Mishnah teaches
a rabbinic change – one that can be reversed,
and all the more so a Torah change;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּנָּא דִּידַן קָתָנֵי שִׁינּוּי דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources speak about different levels of change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה's cases were the basic, Torah-level change, so anything it left out (like sanding) does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches the weaker, reversible change, and the Torah-level change is included all the more.

steps.title: How the משנה's cases are reversible changes
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה's 'wood into vessels' means boards that were already sanded, and 'wool into garments' means wool that was already spun. Both can be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wood that he made into vessels' means sanded wood. What is that? Boards. That is a change that can return to its original state, because if he wants he can take them apart. 'Wool that he made into garments' means spun wool. That is a change that can return to its original state, because if he wants he can unravel it. And all the more so a Torah change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows how the משנה's cases fit his answer. The wood was already sanded boards and the wool was already spun thread, so building or weaving them can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nailing boards together can be undone by pulling them apart, and a garment can be unraveled back into thread. So these are only rabbinic-level changes. This means the משנה never said that sanding raw wood is not a change. It simply started from wood that was already sanded.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool that was already spun into thread

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as stolen raw wood or raw wool. In אביי's reading, the robber stole wood that was already sanded and wool that was already spun.

phrases.english: Wood which he made into vessels –
refers to sanded wood,
and what are they? Boards;
for it is a change that can return to its original state –
since if he wants, he can take them apart.
Wool which he made into garments – refers to spun wool;
for it is a change that can return to its original state –
since if he wants, he can unravel it.
And all the more so a Torah change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the משנה's cases fit אביי's answer in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the cases of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wood and wool were raw materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: The materials were already sanded and spun, so the משנה's changes can be undone and count only מדרבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches only a Torah-level change
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes: the ברייתא teaches only Torah-level changes like sanding and washing, and says nothing about rabbinic-level changes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the outside תנא teaches a Torah change, but he does not teach a rabbinic change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes his answer by explaining what the ברייתא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sanding raw wood or washing raw wool cannot be undone, so it is a שינוי דאורייתא. The ברייתא teaches only that level, so it does not clash with the משנה. The two sources simply cover different levels of change.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'outside' תנא, meaning the author of the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches a change that can be undone (rabbinic level), so a Torah-level change is included all the more. The ברייתא teaches only a change that cannot be undone, like sanding or washing (Torah level). So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: And the tanna of the baraita –
teaches a Torah change,
but does not teach a rabbinic change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by explaining the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source covers a different level of change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה disagree about whether sanding or washing is a change.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches a Torah-level change and the משנה teaches a rabbinic-level change, so they do not disagree.

steps.title: רב אשי: Our משנה also speaks of Torah-level changes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer from אביי. The משנה is talking about changes that cannot be undone: wood made into pestles, and wool made into felt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: our משנה is also talking about a Torah-level change. 'Wood made into vessels' means pestles, which is like sanding. 'Wool made into garments' means felt, which is a change that can't be reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא in a new way. He says both are talking about the same kind of strong, permanent change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the משנה teaches a weaker, rabbinic-level change. רב אשי disagrees: the 'vessels' in the משנה are pestles, which are made by trimming wood, just like sanding. The 'garments' are felt, which can never go back to loose wool. So there is no contradiction, because both sources describe changes that cannot be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: A change that counts by Torah law
A change that cannot go back

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with אביי's answer. אביי said the משנה is about a reversible change, while רב אשי says it is about a permanent one.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The tanna of our Mishnah as well
is teaching a Torah-level change:
'wood that he made into vessels' means pestles,
which is the same as sanding them;
phrases.notes: This is the sanding case from the ברייתא in step 6.

phrases.english: 'wool that he made into garments' means felt,
which is a change that does not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, תַּנָּא דִּידַן נָמֵי שִׁינּוּי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction from step 6, as an alternative to אביי's answer in steps 7-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the cases in the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'vessels' and 'garments' seemed to be weaker changes than sanding or washing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means pestles and felt, which are permanent Torah-level changes, just like the ברייתא.

steps.title: Challenge: Is washing wool really a change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's claim that washing wool is a change. A משנה about ראשית הגז says washed wool must still be given to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does washing really count as a change? There is a contradiction: if he did not give the wool to the כהן before he dyed it, he is exempt. If he washed it but did not dye it, he must still give it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's statement that washing wool counts as a change. It uses a משנה about the first shearings that go to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ראשית הגז, the wool must be given only while it is still basically the same wool. The משנה says dyeing releases the owner, but washing does not, so washing is not a real change. That clashes with the ברייתא, which said washing wool is a change.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.english: But does washing count as a change?
And they raised a contradiction:
If he did not manage to give it to him
phrases.notes: This is about the first shearings, which go to the כהן. 'Him' is the כהן.

phrases.english: before he dyed it, he is exempt.
If he washed it but did not dye it, he is obligated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending our משנה to questioning the ברייתא's claim about washing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that washing wool is a change.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the laws of ראשית הגז, washed wool is still treated as the same wool, so washing is not a change.

steps.title: אביי: A dispute between רבי שמעון and the Sages
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two sources follow different opinions. The ברייתא (washing is a change) follows רבי שמעון, and the משנה about ראשית הגז follows the חכמים. He proves this from another ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: no difficulty. This source is רבי שמעון and that one is the חכמים. A ברייתא teaches: if he sheared, spun and wove it, it does not combine. If he washed it, רבי שמעון says it does not combine, and the חכמים say it does combine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by saying the two sources come from two different תנאים. He brings a ברייתא where they openly argue about washed wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool that has been spun or woven no longer joins other wool to make up the minimum amount for ראשית הגז. About washed wool there is a מחלוקת. רבי שמעון holds washing is a change, matching our ברייתא. The חכמים hold it is not a change, matching the משנה that says the owner must still give it.

keyTerms.meaning: He sheared it, spun it and wove it

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult;
this is Rabbi Shimon, and that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that says washing is a change follows רבי שמעון. The משנה about the כהן follows the Rabbis.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
If he sheared it, spun it and wove it,
it does not combine.
phrases.notes: It does not join the other wool to make up the minimum amount that obligates giving to the כהן.

phrases.aramaic: לִבְּנוֹ – רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מִצְטָרֵף,
phrases.english: If he washed it, Rabbi Shimon says: it does not combine,
and the Sages say: it combines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to give one shared view on whether washing is a change.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds washing is a change, and the חכמים hold it is not. Each source follows one of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether washing counts as a change is itself a מחלוקת among the תנאים.

steps.title: רבא: Both follow רבי שמעון, depending on how the wool was prepared
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sources follow רבי שמעון. In the משנה the wool was only untangled by hand before washing, so the washing is weak. In the ברייתא it was combed, so the washing is a real change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: both this and that follow רבי שמעון, and there is no difficulty. This one is where he untangled the wool, and that one is where he combed it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי. He keeps both sources under one opinion and explains the difference through the details of each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי needed two opinions, but רבא needs only one. If the wool was just pulled apart by hand, the washing does not do much and is not a change, so the owner still gives it to the כהן. If the wool was combed first, the washing works well and counts as a change, just as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: He untangled it (pulled apart by hand)

steps.whatToRemember: On washing wool: אביי says רבי שמעון and the חכמים argue about it. רבא says both sources follow רבי שמעון, and it depends on whether the wool was combed before washing (a change) or only untangled by hand (not a change).

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one and that one both follow Rabbi Shimon,
and it is not difficult;
this is where he untangled it by hand,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about the כהן. The washing does not work well, so it is no change.

phrases.english: that is where he combed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 11's contradiction, as an alternative to אביי in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to need two different opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי שמעון. Washing after combing is a change, and washing after only untangling by hand is not.

steps.title: Light whitening versus strong bleaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין gives a third way to settle the ברייתא and the משנה of ראשית הגז. The משנה is about wool that was only lightly whitened. The ברייתא is about wool that was strongly bleached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said: This source (the משנה) is talking about wool that was only lightly whitened. That source (the ברייתא) is talking about wool that was strongly bleached.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבין gives another answer to the question from Step 11. He says the two sources are talking about two different levels of washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא in Step 13, he keeps both sources inside רבי שמעון's view. But he explains the difference another way. Light whitening is a weak change, so the wool still goes to the כהן. Strong bleaching is a real change.

keyTerms.meaning: He whitened it lightly; a light, simple whitening
He bleached it strongly; a heavy whitening that really changes the wool

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said:
This is where he only lightly whitened it,
phrases.notes: "This" means the משנה of ראשית הגז, where the washed wool still goes to the כהן.

phrases.english: that is where he strongly bleached it.
phrases.notes: "That" means the ברייתא, which says washing counts as a change.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר: הָא דְּחַוְּורֵיהּ חַוּוֹרֵי, הָא דְּכַבְרֵיהּ כַּבְרוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of Step 11, parallel to רבא's answer in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by how strong the washing was
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every kind of washing is the same, so the two sources contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Light whitening is not a change. Strong bleaching is a change.

steps.title: For רבי שמעון even dyeing is not a change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי שמעון holds washing is a change. A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון as saying that even dyed wool still combines for ראשית הגז, so dyeing is not a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, can we really say that for רבי שמעון dyeing is not a change, yet washing is a change? As a ברייתא teaches: If someone sheared his sheep one at a time and dyed the wool, or spun it, or wove it, the wool does not combine. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: if he dyed it, it does combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. A ברייתא shows that for רבי שמעון dyeing is not a change, and dyeing seems much stronger than washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 said that for רבי שמעון washing counts as a change. But here רבי שמעון says dyed wool still combines with other wool, which means dyeing did not change it. If dyeing is not a change, it seems hard to say that washing, which is weaker, is a change.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines, adds up to reach the minimum amount

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. רבי שמעון בן יהודה is a student who is reporting what his teacher רבי שמעון said. The question is about רבי שמעון's own view.

phrases.english: Now, can it be said

phrases.aramaic: צֶבַע לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא הָוֵי שִׁינּוּי,
phrases.english: that according to Rabbi Shimon dyeing is not a change,
yet washing is a change?
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he sheared one by one and dyed it,
phrases.notes: He sheared one sheep, worked on that wool, and only then sheared the next sheep.

phrases.english: one by one and spun it,
one by one and wove it,
it does not combine.
phrases.notes: The wool from the different sheep does not add up to the minimum amount needed for the duty of ראשית הגז.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
if he dyed it, it combines.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר צֶבַע לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא הָוֵי שִׁינּוּי, לִיבּוּן הָוֵי שִׁינּוּי? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the shared premise of Steps 12 and 13, that רבי שמעון holds washing is a change
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for רבי שמעון washing (לִיבּוּן) counts as a change
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dyeing is a stronger change than washing. If רבי שמעון says dyed wool still combines, meaning it is unchanged, then washed wool should surely count as unchanged too.

steps.title: Two students report רבי שמעון differently
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that there are two reports of רבי שמעון's view. The Rabbis report that he holds washing is a change. רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports that he holds even dyeing is not a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is not a problem. This source is the Rabbis reporting רבי שמעון's view. That source is רבי שמעון בן יהודה reporting רבי שמעון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by saying the two sources do not agree on what רבי שמעון held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not try to make the two sources fit together. He says they are two separate traditions about one teacher. In one tradition רבי שמעון treats washing as a change. In the other he does not even treat dyeing as a change.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of; reporting the opinion of

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult;
this is the Rabbis according to Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: This is the source saying washing is a change. It is the Rabbis' report of what רבי שמעון holds.

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: that is Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא רַבָּנַן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the same teacher's view (תרי תנאי אליבא דרבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources give one single view of רבי שמעון, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources disagree about what רבי שמעון held. Each one is a different report of his view.

steps.title: Dye can be washed out, but indigo cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is no argument about רבי שמעון's view: washing is a change. Ordinary dye is a weak change because soap can remove it. The משנה that exempts dyed wool is talking about indigo, which cannot be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the Rabbis do not disagree with רבי שמעון בן יהודה. Dye is different, because you can remove it with soap. And when the משנה there teaches, "He did not manage to give it to the כהן until he dyed it, he is exempt," and we said that rule is everyone's opinion, it is talking about indigo, which does not come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי. He says all the reports of רבי שמעון agree, and ordinary dye is simply a weaker change than washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dye can be scrubbed off with soap, so the wool can go back to how it was. That makes it a weak change, even though washing is a real one. רבא then deals with a problem: a משנה says dyed wool is exempt from ראשית הגז, which shows dyeing is a change. He explains that this משנה is talking about indigo, a dye that cannot be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of soap or cleaning material that can remove dye
Indigo, a blue dye that does not wash out
We explained it as talking about a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. אביי says the reports of רבי שמעון's view disagree. רבא says they agree: washing is a change, ordinary dye is not a change because soap removes it, and indigo is a change because it is permanent.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer gives a clear test for a real change: can it be undone? A change that can be reversed is weak. A permanent change counts. This fits רב אשי's idea in Step 10.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, the Rabbis do not disagree
with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda,
but dye is different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לְהַעֲבִירוֹ עַל יְדֵי צָפוֹן.
phrases.english: since one can remove it with soap.
And when it teaches there:
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה about ראשית הגז.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לִיתְּנוֹ לוֹ עַד שֶׁצְּבָעוֹ – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: "He did not manage to give it to him until he dyed it, he is exempt,"
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן who should have received the first shearing.

phrases.english: and we established it as the view of everyone;
that is about indigo, which does not come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the קשיא of Step 15, disagreeing with אביי's answer in Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the cases are different (reversible dye versus permanent dye), with a limiting reading of another משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dye is a stronger change than washing, so if dye is not a change, washing cannot be one
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary dye is weak because it can be removed. Washing is a real change. Indigo, which is permanent, is also a real change.

steps.title: אביי lists five תנאים who hold that a change does not alter status
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי שמעון בן יהודה, בית שמאי, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and רבי ישמעאל all hold שינוי במקומו עומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, בית שמאי, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and רבי ישמעאל all hold that a changed item stays in its place. It keeps the status it had before the change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a new general statement: five different תנאים all share one opinion, that changing an item does not change its legal status. This opens a new section where the גמרא proves each name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא focused on whether a change, such as washing or dyeing wool, counts as a real change. אביי now steps back and groups together the תנאים who hold that a change does not affect the item's status. The steps that follow will prove each name on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, 'a change stands in its place.' The changed item keeps its original status.
A change in the item's form

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip this! שינוי במקומו עומד means the change does NOT matter. The item is treated as if it never changed. It is the opposite of saying a change creates something new.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the section. Each name on the list will be backed up with a source.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, and Beit Shammai,
and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר, וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל –
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, and Rabbi Yishmael –
all of them hold:
a changed item stays in its place.
phrases.notes: In other words, after the change the item still has its old status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific question about רבי שמעון's view on wool to a general list of תנאים who hold that a change does not alter status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five תנאים all hold שינוי במקומו עומד.

steps.title: The source for רבי שמעון בן יהודה is what was already said
steps.stepSummary: The proof for רבי שמעון בן יהודה is his report, already quoted, that even dyed wool still combines for ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה: that is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first name on אביי's list. It points back to a source we already saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבי שמעון בן יהודה reported that even dyed wool still counts toward ראשית הגז. Since even dyeing does not change the wool's status, that view fits the idea that a change does not alter status.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing of wool, which is given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda – that which we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 15, where he said even dyed wool still counts for ראשית הגז.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first name on אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds שינוי במקומו עומד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His report in step 15 that, according to רבי שמעון, even dyed wool still combines for ראשית הגז.

steps.title: What is the source for בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that בית שמאי hold that a change does not alter status.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי: what is the source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second name on the list and asks for the proof. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי שמעון בן יהודה, the view of בית שמאי has not appeared yet in the סוגיא. So the גמרא has to bring a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request for the source

phrases.english: Beit Shammai – what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we see that בית שמאי hold this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first name to the second name on אביי's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that בית שמאי hold שינוי במקומו עומד.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about a prostitute's payment that she changed
steps.stepSummary: A prostitute was paid with wheat, olives or grapes and turned them into flour, oil or wine. One ברייתא forbids bringing them on the מזבח, and another permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: if he gave her wheat as her payment and she made it into flour, or olives and she made them into oil, or grapes and she made them into wine, one ברייתא teaches that it is forbidden and another ברייתא teaches that it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for בית שמאי. It starts with two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about an אתנן that was changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids bringing an אתנן onto the מזבח (דברים 23:19). The question is whether turning the item into something new, such as wheat into flour, removes the ban. The ברייתא that forbids it treats the item as unchanged, and the one that permits it treats the change as real. The גמרא will soon explain whose views these are.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given to a prostitute, which may not be brought to the מקדש
One ברייתא teaches, and another ברייתא teaches. This signals a contradiction between sources.

phrases.english: As it is taught: if he gave her wheat as her payment,
phrases.notes: "Her" is a prostitute. The Torah bans her payment from the מזבח (דברים 23:19).

phrases.english: and she made it into flour;
olives, and she made them into oil;
grapes, and she made them into wine –
one ברייתא teaches: it is forbidden,
and another ברייתא teaches: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by bringing the source material.
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי hold שינוי במקומו עומד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות about a changed אתנן. Their contradiction will be resolved by attributing the strict one to בית שמאי.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins to resolve the two ברייתות by quoting גוריון
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף starts to settle the contradiction by quoting a teaching of גוריון. The teaching continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: גוריון taught...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins his answer to the contradiction between the two ברייתות. This line only introduces his answer, and the actual explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction between "forbidden" and "permitted" needs a solution. רב יוסף will bring a teaching from גוריון to show which תנאים each ברייתא follows. That is how the proof for בית שמאי will be completed.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose teaching רב יוסף quotes

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: Guryon taught

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to resolve the contradiction between the two ברייתות in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each ברייתא to a different תנא (still being introduced)
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet given. רב יוסף's quote from גוריון continues after this point.
